newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power mostly steady on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power mostly steady on mild weather.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady Tuesday, maintained at moderate levels by mild weather, industry sources said.
Most traders said they expected spot power prices to move higher next week, as forecasts called for some below-normal temperatures through a good portion of the Midwest.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power deals for Wednesday delivery were pegged steady at $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In MAIN, peak, non-firm power for Wednesday delivery was pegged relatively steady at $20.00-21.00 from $19.50-22.00 on Monday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
January/February MAIN peak power was said to be talked steady at $25.50-26.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday were discussed lower at $18.00-19.00 from $19.00-20.00 on Monday for Tuesday delivery, the sources said.
Off-peak, non-firm next-day ECAR power was assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
January/February peak ECAR prices were pegged steady at $23.75-24.25 per MWh.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were talked steady at $16.00-17.00, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were said to be lower in the $11.00-13.00 range from $13.00-15.00 on Monday.
January/February peak SPP power was pegged steady at $24.75-25.25, the sources said.
